dedupe_keys.name: front range flood colorado september 2013 dam safety response and uncontrolled irrigation ditch inflows asdso case study

description: This case study from the Association of State Dam Safety Officials, drawing on the Colorado Dam Safety Branch, reconstructs the timeline of the 8 to 18 September 2013 storm that dropped up to 17 inches of rain over seven days along Colorado's Front Range, and the state's response for its more than 1,700 regulated dams. It records that high and significant hazard dams performed as designed, that nine small low hazard dams failed, and that flood damage to river diversion structures let uncontrolled water into irrigation ditches, some of which failed and flooded developed areas, while reservoirs spilling for the first time led residents to report false dam failures. It also describes how 113 volunteer engineers from 27 firms and five agencies completed emergency inspections within six days. Coverage: one regional event; text, photographs and lessons learned. Access: a free web page; the licence is not stated. Caveats: narrative, not data, with no downloadable inspection results on the page. It supports studies of coupled irrigation and dam failure, emergency response and inspection surge capacity, and relates to the ASDSO warning lessons and incident database in the catalogue.
